messages:
Alex R: quick heads-up — fp8 bring-up (mistral-variant) showing structured tool-call failures on our function-calling eval set. started with a small bakeoff vs int8/gptq.
Priya K: ugh, reproducible? can you paste an example failure (raw output)?
Alex R: yes — most failures are JSON parse errors or truncated arrays in 'tool_args'. example:
```
Assistant: {"tool":"fetch_price","args":["BTC","USD"]}
Assistant: {"tool":"fetch_price","args":["BTC","USD"  <-- truncated
```
these only appear on fp8 builds; int8/gptq looks cleaner.
Jay M: that's symptomatic of tokenization/kv-cache truncation or EOS handling during decoding. any logs of final token stream?
Alex R: attaching snippet of generation tokens (manual redact):
```
... 50256 35 999 1 50256 2  
```
weird double-EOS (50256) in the middle of sequences for fp8 run.
Sophie L: double-EOS could cause output cut-off, leading to malformed JSON. do we have beam/search differences? which sampler?
Alex R: greedy for eval harness. hypothesis: quantization noise in softmax causes spurious EOS probs earlier.
Zane: interesting — on quantized models softmax/shadow-exponent can underflow/overflow. fp8 kernels sometimes fuse operations and change numerics. have we tried forcing fp32 for the final layer?
Priya K: I ran an A/B with final-layer-fp32 (runtime override) on a small slice. results:
- fp32 baseline: JSON validity 99.8%
- fp8 default: JSON validity 94.6% (EM drop ~3.2 pts on tool-args schema)
- fp8 + final-layer-fp32: JSON validity 99.1%
so final-layer float seems to recover most of the regression.
Jay M: that's a strong signal. can we quantify impact on latency/cost for that mitigation? what's perf delta?
Alex R: perf: +6% latency median, +3% token-cost (on dedicated A100 pool) — acceptable for canary.
Sophie L: do we see same with AWQ/GPTQ? maybe only fp8 fused kernels cause the issue.
Priya K: AWQ/gptq int8 runs show ~98.9% JSON validity, small delta vs fp32. AWQ had slightly different tokenization alignment but no double-EOS.
Zane: plan: patch runtime to allow final-layer-fp32 flag per model; run canary on dedicated cluster with 5% traffic. deploy-bot can schedule.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: redwood-canary-eng-ml / fp8-finalfp32-5pct -> starting at 2026-03-21T09:30Z. (ID: cb-1773006799)
Alex R: excellent. follow-ups:
- Priya: run full eval suite (10k tool-calls) with final-layer-fp32 and capture per-route EM/JSON-validity
- Jay: add telemetry to log token-stream around EOS for quantized variants (sampled)
- Sophie: update our quantization docs with a note about final-layer precision for structured-output models
- Zane: add runtime flag and config validation
Priya K: running eval now. preliminary numbers look promising; will attach CSV in thread when done.
Jay M: also let's add a quick unit in the harness that rejects outputs with mismatched bracket counts before parsing (temporary guard).
Alex R: agreed — I pushed a tiny patch to harness: if bracket mismatch -> mark as invalid and increment metric rather than crash parser.
Sophie L: thanks team. if canary is green after 2 hours we can roll to 20% and then full. keep an eye on cost delta and tail latency.
Zane: noted. I'll open an RFC for the runtime flag and link to this thread.
Priya K: CSV uploaded: gist.redwood/snapshots/1773006901 (contains per-model, per-quant table). early summary: final-layer-fp32 recovers 85-95% of regression across tasks.
Alex R: awesome. closing action: monitor canary and collect error-rate per-route. if regression persists on any route, we'll pin that route to int8/gptq for now and queue follow-up work to debug fp8 kernel numerics.
Sophie L: +1 :thumbsup:
Zane: RFC opened: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/823 — includes perf numbers and proposed config schema.
deploy-bot: canary: cb-1773006799 -> healthy at 11:45Z, json-validity metric improved to 99.0% on fp8-finalfp32.
Alex R: thanks all — great triage. we'll reconvene if anything flares.
